youtube_title: How does Autonomous Emergency Braking work? AEB explained
caption:
Guess before the reveal 👀 Which one can AEB miss most easily?

A) Stopped car ahead
B) Bike cutting in
C) Slow truck ahead

Autonomous Emergency Braking uses radar and/or a camera to spot a hazard, warn you, and then brake if you don't react. It's genuinely useful, but Indian roads throw a lot at it.

Comment your answer before you watch the end.

slides.heading: What can your AEB easily miss?
A sudden bike cut-in
slides.body: The sensors need a moment to confirm a hazard. A bike cutting in close leaves almost no time.

slides.heading: How AEB works
slides.body: Radar or camera spots a hazard, warns you first, then brakes if you don't react.

slides.heading: Also tricky: cattle, night, rain
slides.body: Odd shapes, pedestrians in low light and heavy rain can confuse the sensors.

slides.heading: AEB is a backup
slides.body: Keep a 3-second gap and cover the brake near bikes. Never rely on it to stop for you.

voice_lines: What can your AEB easily miss? It's a bike suddenly cutting in, because the system gets almost no time to react.
Here's how it works. Radar or a camera spots something ahead, warns you first, then brakes if you don't.
Indian roads add more trouble, like cattle, people crossing at night and heavy rain, which can confuse the sensors.
So treat AEB as a backup, keep a three second gap, and follow for more car safety tech.
